description: Machine-readable copy rules for the Stigmer sales website. Defines voice, banned phrases, required writing patterns, and terminology enforcement. Used by lint tooling (site/scripts/lint-copy.ts) and Cursor rules (.cursor/rules/site/) to enforce copy quality.

confident_not_arrogant.description: State what Stigmer does well. Be transparent about where it is headed.

technical_not_academic.description: Use precise terms. Avoid jargon that adds no information.

conversational_not_casual.description: Write as if speaking to a peer at a technical meetup.

active_voice.description: Always active voice. 'Stigmer runs your agent,' not 'Your agent is run by Stigmer.'

banned_phrases.replacement: State the specific capability (HA, RBAC, audit logs)

banned_phrases.reason: Subjective — developers will verify and disagree
Corporate jargon — signals marketing over engineering
The entire product is AI-related — adds no information

banned_phrases.replacement: Use 'use' or state the specific action
State the specific advantage with proof
Name the specific technology or approach

every_claim_needs_proof.description: No undemonstrated assertions. Every claim must be accompanied by a code snippet, terminal output, metric, or link.

code_before_paragraph.description: When explaining a capability, show the code first, then explain.

specific_numbers_over_adjectives.description: '5 lines of YAML' beats 'simple configuration.' Every quantifiable claim must use a number.

feature_benefit_proof_structure.description: Every feature follows: (1) Benefit — why it matters, (2) Feature — what it is, (3) Proof — code, metric, or link. Lead with the benefit.

objection_aware_writing.description: Anticipate why the visitor might leave and address it directly.

honest_comparisons.description: When comparing to alternatives, state genuine differences. Acknowledge competitor strengths. Never misrepresent.

sales_terminology.context: Use the domain model term. The sales site must not introduce terminology that contradicts the domain model.
A single invocation of an agent. Use the canonical term from the proto model.
MCP tool integration definition. Use the protocol name.
